questions.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
questions.learningObjective: identify an appropriate strategy for handling missing data
questions.stem: A column in a dataset has 5 percent of its values missing at random. Which strategy is most defensible before modelling?

options.text: Impute using the column median and flag the imputed rows
Delete every row that has any missing value
options.misconception: discards too much data when missingness is small and random
injects a value that may be far from the true distribution

options.text: Ignore the missing values and fit the model anyway
options.misconception: assumes most algorithms handle missing data by default

questions.explanation: When missingness is small and random, median imputation preserves the distribution while a flag lets the model learn that the value was imputed. Listwise deletion wastes data, zero filling distorts the distribution, and most algorithms do not silently skip missing values, which is why option D is the most dangerous of the four.

questions.learningObjective: classify a column as nominal, ordinal, interval, or ratio
questions.stem: Which measurement scale best describes temperature in degrees Celsius?

options.misconception: confuses a quantity with a category
treats equal intervals as mere ordering
ignores the meaningful zero at absolute zero only

questions.explanation: Celsius has equal intervals between values but no true zero, so it is interval. Ratio requires a true zero, nominal has no order, and ordinal lacks equal intervals, which is why option D is correct.

questions.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
questions.learningObjective: choose an appropriate transformation for a skewed distribution
questions.stem: A right-skewed positive variable has a long tail. Which transformation most commonly stabilizes variance and reduces skew?

options.misconception: amplifies the skew rather than reducing it
shifts location without changing shape
overcomplicates and inverts the relationship

questions.explanation: The logarithm compresses the upper tail of a positive right-skewed variable, reducing skew and stabilizing variance. Squaring worsens skew, adding a constant only shifts location, and an unnecessary reciprocal adds complexity without benefit.

questions.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
questions.learningObjective: compute the interquartile range fence for outlier detection
questions.stem: For a column, Q1 is 10 and Q3 is 20. What is the upper outlier fence using 1.5 times the IQR?
questions.explanation: The IQR is Q3 minus Q1, which is 10. Multiplying by 1.5 gives 15, and adding to Q3 gives 35. Values above this fence are flagged as outliers under the standard Tukey rule.

questions.stem: Min-max scaling maps a value x to (x - min)/(max - min). For min=2, max=12, and x=7, what is the scaled value?
questions.explanation: Subtracting the minimum gives 5, and the range is 10, so the scaled value is 0.5. Min-max scaling places the value at the midpoint of the new zero-to-one range.

questions.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
questions.learningObjective: evaluate the risk of mean imputation on variance
questions.stem: What is a known downside of mean imputation for a numeric column?

options.text: It increases the variance of the column
options.misconception: mean imputation shrinks variance instead

options.text: It reduces the variance of the column

options.misconception: only missing entries are altered

options.text: It requires the column to be categorical
options.misconception: confuses imputation with encoding

questions.explanation: Mean imputation replaces missing values with the average, which pulls imputed points toward the center and artificially reduces variance. It does not touch observed values, does not require categoricals, and does not increase variance.

questions.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
questions.learningObjective: select a robust central tendency measure in the presence of outliers
questions.stem: A column has extreme outliers. Which measure of center is most robust?

options.misconception: the mean is pulled toward extreme values
useful for categoricals, not robust for numeric tails
depends entirely on the two extremes

questions.explanation: The median depends only on the middle order statistic, so extreme values barely affect it. The mean is sensitive to extremes, the mode is not a reliable numeric center, and the range midpoint is driven by the two outliers themselves.

questions.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
questions.learningObjective: recognize when standardization is preferred over min-max scaling
questions.stem: When is z-score standardization generally preferred over min-max scaling?

options.text: When the algorithm assumes Gaussian-like input or uses distance with outliers
When all values must lie strictly between 0 and 1
options.misconception: that is the min-max use case
neither scaling applies to categoricals

options.text: When there are no missing values
options.misconception: missingness is unrelated to scaling choice

questions.explanation: Z-score standardization centers on the mean with unit variance, which suits algorithms expecting roughly Gaussian input and is less distorted by extreme values than min-max. Min-max is for bounded ranges, scaling does not apply to categoricals, and missingness does not determine the scaling method.

questions.learningObjective: compare listwise deletion versus imputation tradeoffs
questions.stem: When is listwise deletion of rows with missing values most acceptable?

options.text: When missingness is small and completely random
When missingness exceeds 40 percent of rows

options.misconception: deleting labeled rows can bias the sample

options.text: When the data is time series

questions.learningObjective: compute the z-score of a value
questions.stem: A value is 14, the mean is 10, and the standard deviation is 2. What is its z-score?
